2874.english: to drop or decline in regional usage
first: 方言中的落低可以表示下降。
fāng yán zhōng de luò dī kě yǐ biǎo shì xià jiàng.
In regional usage, luo di can mean to drop or decline.
second: 这份方言材料用落低说明水位下降。
zhè fèn fāng yán cái liào yòng luò dī shuō míng shuǐ wèi xià jiàng.
This dialect material uses luo di to describe a falling water level.
2874.note: Regional Southern Min usage reported as lak-kē; the displayed pinyin gives Mandarin character readings, not its local pronunciation. The examples discuss this dialect term in Mandarin.
2874.source: Usage checked against iTaigi https://itaigi.tw/k/下落/ (entry 落低, citing 台文華文線頂辭典); English explanation and both examples newly authored.

4863.english: slippery and difficult to walk on
first: 方言记录中的滑跶形容路面滑溜。
fāng yán jì lù zhōng de huá dá xíng róng lù miàn huá liu.
In the dialect record, hua da describes a slippery walking surface.
second: 雨后的石路滑跶，走时要小心。
yǔ hòu de shí lù huá dá, zǒu shí yào xiǎo xīn.
The stone path is slippery after the rain, so walk carefully.
4863.note: Older Wu/Shanghai regional expression. The pinyin transcribes Mandarin character readings rather than Shanghai pronunciation; common Mandarin uses 滑溜 or 容易打滑.
4863.source: Attestation checked in Ye Shisun, Xinmin Evening News, 2020-01-19 https://paper.xinmin.cn/html/xmwb/2020-01-19/19/55584.html ; English paraphrase and examples newly authored.
